normalization.note: All input text is lowercased before matching. Substring matching is applied without stemming or lemmatisation.

severityBands.clinicalMeaning: No significant concern signal in the analyzed window.
Mild concern or repeated low-level markers.
severityBands.defaultAction: Show in dashboard and include in clinician digest.

severityBands.clinicalMeaning: Moderate concern or explicit self-harm marker requiring same-day review.
severityBands.defaultAction: Same-day clinician review and acknowledgement required.

severityBands.clinicalMeaning: High concern, plan/preparation marker, or multi-vector escalation.
severityBands.defaultAction: Immediate human review and urgent clinician alert required.

categories.whyItMatters: General distress language indicates emotional pain that, while common, may escalate if left unaddressed. Early detection supports timely check-ins before a low-level state worsens.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your recent messages contained language associated with emotional distress. This is a supportive signal, not a judgment about your character.
exclusionNotes: Exclude when used in clearly hypothetical or fictional contexts.
Exclude colloquial intensifiers such as 'this exam is killing me' that lack broader affective context.
Exclude single isolated complaints without co-occurring distress signals.
terms: i feel like i'm falling apart
i feel so alone in this
i'm tired of feeling this way
life feels so heavy right now
i feel worn down to nothing

categories.whyItMatters: Language indicating deterioration over time suggests that prior coping strategies may be failing and that clinical attention is warranted before the trajectory becomes acute.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages reflected a pattern suggesting your wellbeing may be declining compared to previous entries. Speaking to someone who can help is a good next step.
exclusionNotes: Exclude references to physical illness worsening unless co-occurring with emotional distress signals.
Exclude academic performance language alone such as 'my grades are getting worse' without emotional context.
terms: it's been getting harder each day
i can't bounce back like i used to
i'm struggling more than last week
each day is harder than the last
it's beyond what i can handle now
i'm further away from okay than before

categories.whyItMatters: Social withdrawal is a recognized early behavioral indicator of depression and other mood disorders. Reduced interpersonal contact can accelerate isolation and remove protective support networks.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your recent messages suggest you may be withdrawing from social contact. Connection to others is one of the strongest protective factors for wellbeing.
exclusionNotes: Exclude intentional solitude for studying or personal preference when expressed positively.
Exclude introversion self-identification without associated distress language.

i avoid eye contact with everyone
i don't feel like socializing at all

i don't leave my room anymore

categories.whyItMatters: Hopelessness is one of the strongest cognitive predictors of suicidal ideation identified in clinical research. Early detection allows for timely cognitive and emotional intervention.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages contained language expressing a loss of hope about the future. Reaching out to support services can help shift this perspective.
exclusionNotes: Exclude situational hopelessness about a specific exam or event without broader life context.
Exclude rhetorical or hyperbolic expressions clearly used for emphasis in casual conversation without other distress signals.

categories.whyItMatters: Perceived burdensomenessâ€”the belief that one is a burden to othersâ€”is a significant risk factor in the interpersonal theory of suicidal behavior and warrants careful monitoring.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages suggest you may feel like a burden to those around you. This perception is common but often untrue, and support is available to help you work through it.
exclusionNotes: Exclude expressions of guilt about minor inconveniences without self-deprecatory or suicidal context.
Exclude references to financial burden on family in a purely practical context without emotional distress co-occurring.

categories.whyItMatters: Absolutist and all-or-nothing thinking patterns are associated with depression and cognitive distortions. They can amplify emotional distress and significantly reduce problem-solving capacity.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages contained language reflecting all-or-nothing thinking, which is a recognized sign of cognitive distress that can be addressed through support.
exclusionNotes: Exclude superlatives used in clearly positive or humorous contexts.
Exclude absolute language in academic or factual statements unrelated to personal emotional state.
terms: nothing ever works out for me
i'm never going to be better
i'll never be happy no matter what

categories.whyItMatters: Disrupted sleep is both a symptom and an amplifier of mood disorders. Persistent sleep problems can accelerate emotional deterioration and reduce the capacity for emotional regulation.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your entries suggest you may be experiencing sleep difficulties. Sleep is closely linked to emotional wellbeing and recovery.
exclusionNotes: Exclude one-off mentions of staying up late for studying without distress context.
Exclude travel-related sleep disruption described neutrally.
Extreme sleep disruption is captured separately in the extreme_sleep_disruption category.

categories.whyItMatters: Anxiety and panic symptoms can significantly impair daily functioning and, when severe or untreated, increase risk for both mental and physical health complications including crisis escalation.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages suggested possible anxiety or panic experiences. Support resources specifically for anxiety are available through the platform.
exclusionNotes: Exclude casual use of 'anxious' or 'stressed' about specific low-stakes events without physical symptom language.
Exclude self-reported past history of panic without present-tense symptoms in the current entry.

categories.whyItMatters: Elevated anger and irritability can indicate mood instability associated with depressive or mixed episodes. It can also predict impulsive behavior and relationship breakdown that removes protective support.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages reflected heightened anger or irritability. These emotions, when intense or persistent, can signal underlying distress worth addressing.
exclusionNotes: Exclude isolated venting about a specific frustrating event without broader emotional context.
Exclude humor-coded complaints such as 'my professor is driving me crazy lol' without affective elaboration.

categories.whyItMatters: Substance use as a coping mechanism substantially elevates mental health risk and can mask or worsen underlying conditions. It may also interact dangerously with prescribed psychiatric medications.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages suggested possible substance use related to managing emotional distress. Confidential support for substance concerns is available.
exclusionNotes: Exclude casual social references to alcohol without distress context.
Exclude purely informational or academic references to substances.
Exclude references to past use described in a recovery or sobriety context.

categories.whyItMatters: Abrupt discontinuation or irregular use of psychiatric medications is associated with rapid symptomatic deterioration, discontinuation syndromes, and markedly elevated crisis risk.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages suggested possible changes to how you are managing your prescribed medication. Discussing any changes with your prescriber is important for your safety.
exclusionNotes: Exclude references to physical medications such as antibiotics without psychiatric context.
Exclude planned, provider-directed medication changes described positively.
Exclude hypothetical or general statements about medication compliance in academic discussions.

categories.whyItMatters: Sudden, acute worsening of mental state can precede crisis events. Rapid deterioration signals require urgent response even without explicit suicidal language because the trajectory itself constitutes a safety signal.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your recent messages reflect a sudden and significant decline in your wellbeing. Immediate support is available and strongly encouraged.
exclusionNotes: Exclude isolated acute stress reactions to single external events without personal emotional elaboration.
Exclude dramatic language used habitually in positive or humorous social contexts.

exclusionNotes: Exclude the word 'crisis' in clearly academic or third-party-event contexts.
Exclude crisis language referring to external events such as a 'housing crisis' without personal emotional elaboration.

categories.whyItMatters: Self-harm language indicates a significant safety concern requiring immediate system response. This category triggers safety protocols independent of the total cumulative score and must never be suppressed by protective factors.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages contained language associated with self-harm. Immediate support is available. You are not alone and help is ready when you reach out.
exclusionNotes: Exclude clearly metaphorical use such as 'I worked myself to death' without any physical harm context.
Do not include operational or instructional content of any kind in this category.
Separate from plan_preparation: this category captures general self-harm language and urges, not forward-planning intent.

categories.whyItMatters: Language suggesting a specific plan or preparation for self-harm or suicide is the highest-risk signal in this system and mandates immediate escalation regardless of all other scores. The presence of planning intent is a critical clinical escalator.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages contained language that may indicate thinking about acting on harmful thoughts. Please reach out to crisis support immediately. You matter and help is available now.
exclusionNotes: This category must never include operational, methodological, or instructional details of any kind.
Terms are restricted to expressions of intent, planning behaviour, or preparation without describing any means or methods.
Separate from self_harm: this category is specifically for expressed intent and forward-planning language, not general harm behaviors or urges.

categories.whyItMatters: Protective language indicates active coping resources, social support, future orientation, and reasons for living that are associated with reduced risk and greater resilience. Detecting these signals supports positive reinforcement within the platform.
categories.privacySnippetTemplate: Your messages reflected positive coping language and protective factors. These are meaningful signs of resilience and are noted with care.
exclusionNotes: Exclude performative positivity that co-occurs with high-risk language in the same session entry.
Exclude generic optimism phrases without personal or behavioral anchoring.
Protective factor scores must never suppress mandatory escalation from self_harm or plan_preparation category matches.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Current mood is at least 2 points below the patient's 30-day mean.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Mood rating dropped significantly from the patient's baseline.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Latest mood rating is 2 or below on the 1-5 scale.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Recent mood rating was in the low range.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Sleep hours <= 4 on the latest log or 7-day rolling average.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Sleep duration was repeatedly low in recent logs.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Patient marks prescribed medication as not taken for a scheduled day.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Medication was not marked as taken for a scheduled dose/day.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: 2 or more dose-level missed/skipped/not_taken events in the last 14 days.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Dose-level adherence logs show repeated missed dose events.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: 3 or more dose-level late events in the last 14 days.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Dose-level adherence logs show repeated late dose events.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Guardian medication status contradicts patient medication status for the same date.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Guardian verification conflicts with patient medication self-report.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Guardian-observed mood rating is 1 or 2 on the 1-5 scale.
Appointment status is absent, or a scheduled appointment date is in the past.
2 or more rescheduled appointments or reschedule requests in the analysis window.
3 or more activity events between 01:00 and 05:00 UTC in the analysis window.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Late-night activity increased compared with the patient baseline.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: No patient activity detected for 7 or more consecutive days.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: No recent patient activity was detected.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Latest mobility radius is 50% or less of the 30-day baseline average.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: GPS mobility radius dropped compared with the patient baseline.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Home-stay ratio >= 0.9 in the latest geolocation reading.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: GPS data suggests unusually high home-stay time.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Typing cadence variance > 1000ms AND average IKI < 200ms in the latest diary session.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Detected erratic rapid typing cadence consistent with psychomotor agitation.

nonLexiconSignals.rule: Average IKI > 400ms AND backspace ratio > 0.15 in the latest diary session.
nonLexiconSignals.privacySnippetTemplate: Detected slow hesitant typing cadence consistent with psychomotor retardation.
